_note: Single source of truth. EVERY value traces to a trade-model run (offseason/scripts). The model is seeded/deterministic. See claims.json. Deal: MIN sends Randle for Nembhard + Toppin (Indiana). Thesis: good now AND keeps the 2027 picks.
hook_quote: The smartest Wolves trade nobody is talking about.
hook_sub: Randle for Andrew Nembhard and Obi Toppin. Better now, and it keeps the 2027 picks. I ran it through the model.

deal.picks_note: vs the two firsts a Giddey- or Turner-type deal costs

min.hard_cap_note: A near-even swap that sheds a hair of salary, so it never trips a hard cap.

ind.qualitative: Retooling. Takes Randle's expiring back, lands ~$201M.

title.floor_note: every view lands positive. even the cautious one (+1.0). the best floor of any realistic Wolves deal.
title.metric: modeled championship probability, four-view range (validated 2-for-2 sim)

ind.why: Toppin sits behind Pascal Siakam at the four, so he's the movable one. But Nembhard is a real starter, and parting with two rotation players for an aging Randle is a tougher sell than my model's tidy yes.
ind.margin_note: The model says yes because it grades Nembhard as a below-market contract. read that two ways: Minnesota is probably getting a steal, and a real Indiana likely wants more than Randle, Shannon, and one pick.

min.why: Nembhard fills the half-court playmaking Minnesota lacks. a real need, addressed.
min.channel: fills the need, best cautious-view floor on the board

sayyes.disclaimer: Acceptance is my model's read on willingness, not a report that anyone is shopping these players.

verdict.call: Better now without mortgaging 2027. A high-floor playmaker for an expiring and one pick, with the war chest still intact.
verdict.question: Wolves fans: smarter than chasing a star?
